title: Thyme gargle for sore throat
subtitle: A strong thyme decoction used as a gargle
excerpt: A strong thyme decoction cooled to a comfortable temperature and used as a gargle for a sore, inflamed throat. Two teaspoons of dried thyme simmered covered in 250 ml of water for fifteen minutes, then strained and cooled. Gargle for thirty seconds and spit out. Not for swallowing.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), thyme entry: records the gargle use of strong thyme infusion or decoction for sore throat. Culpeper, The English Physician (1652), thyme entry: documents use for throat complaints. BHP (1983) thyme monograph: dosing reference. EMA HMPC monograph on Thymi herba (2013): safety note on pregnancy at therapeutic doses.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The prepared gargle liquid can be made in a single batch and stored in a glass jar in the fridge for up to 24 hours. Reheat gently to a comfortable temperature before each gargle session. Prepare fresh each day.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Store in a clean covered glass jar in the fridge for up to 24 hours. Discard any unused liquid after one day.

glossaryTerms.definition: A preparation made by simmering harder plant material in water, covered, for fifteen to twenty minutes. Used when a simple infusion would not extract enough from stems or in cases where a stronger concentration is needed.
A preparation held at the back of the throat and gargled for thirty seconds, then spat out. Never swallowed at therapeutic-strength concentrations.

cooled to a comfortable temperature and used as a

for an inflamed, sore throat. Western herbalists draw on thyme's antimicrobial and astringent properties for throat work; a gargle puts the preparation in direct contact with the sore tissue rather than diluting it through the digestive system. Two teaspoons of dried thyme simmered covered in 250 ml of water for fifteen minutes, then strained and cooled, gives enough liquid for three to four gargle sessions. This preparation is to be gargled and spat out; it is not for swallowing.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body:
Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor for ongoing or serious symptoms.

Do NOT swallow this gargle. This is a therapeutic-strength preparation that is much more concentrated than a culinary cup of thyme tea. Gargle and spit out each time.

Pregnancy: culinary use of thyme in cooking is well tolerated. A therapeutic-strength preparation used regularly is a different matter. Consult a herbalist or your midwife before using this remedy in pregnancy.

Paediatric use is not adult-divided-by-half. Consult a herbalist who specialises in children's herbal medicine, or a paediatric doctor, before using any herbal preparation in children under twelve. Children who cannot reliably spit out a gargle should not use a gargle preparation.

content.text: Put 2 teaspoons of dried thyme into a small saucepan. Add 250 ml of cold water.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover with a lid, and simmer for 15 minutes. The liquid reduces a little and deepens in colour and aroma.
Remove from the heat. Strain through a sieve into a clean glass or jug.
Cool to a comfortable gargling temperature: warm but not hot to the touch, so it will not scald the throat.
Take a small mouthful, tilt the head back, gargle for 30 seconds, and spit out. Repeat until you have used one session's worth of liquid (roughly 60 to 80 ml).
Gargle three to four times a day, for the duration of symptoms, up to seven days. Always spit out the gargle liquid. If the sore throat has not improved after five days, or worsens, see a doctor.
The prepared gargle liquid keeps in a clean covered glass jar in the fridge for up to 24 hours. Warm to a comfortable temperature before each gargle session. Make a fresh batch each day.
When not to use this remedy
See a doctor for a sore throat lasting more than a week. Very severe pain, difficulty swallowing or breathing, drooling, a hot lump in the neck, or a high fever.
Do not use this gargle in children who cannot reliably spit out the liquid. Consult a herbalist or your midwife before use in pregnancy.

items.symptom: Gargle is very harsh or stings the throat
items.cause: Liquid is too concentrated or too hot
items.fix: Make sure the liquid is at a comfortable warm temperature before gargling. If it is very concentrated from extended simmering, dilute with a little boiled water before use.

items.symptom: Very little aroma or flavour in the decoction
items.cause: Dried thyme is old or stored in the light
items.fix: Replace with fresh dried thyme. It should smell strongly of thyme when rubbed between fingers.
